children: Howmet Aerospace Inc. (HWM, Financials) The maker of aerospace and industrial components is down almost 20% from its previous record high as investors responded to plans by SpaceX to make gas-turbine components in-house. Citi believes the selloff has gone too far.
The bank put Howmet on a 30-day upside catalyst watch, maintaining a Buy rating and a $329 price target, representing around 34% upside from Monday's $244.95 close.
The concern is simple. Elon Musk revealed that SpaceX aims to cast turbine blades and vanes in-house to enable a 20-gigawatt power plant for AI data centers in Texas.
Citi, however, views this as a sign of limited industry capacity rather than a direct danger to Howmet.
The bank said SpaceX is developing mostly for its own requirements and still planned to rely on the existing turbine supply chain.
This important because Howmet's gas-turbine industry is already expanding fast. First quarter revenue for the category surged 39% following a 25% increase in 2025.
Bernstein made a similar conclusion, raising its Howmet price objective to $328 from $248.
Howmet is also growing turbine blade capacity, with planned expansions that could increase capacity by as much as 38% from first-quarter 2025 levels.
The investment concern today is whether SpaceX will be a true rival or will just confirm that AI-powered electricity demand is outpacing availability of turbine capacity.

title: Howmet Plunged 20% on SpaceX Fears. Citi Says Buy the Dip
